items.problem: UWP app-lifecycle suspend/resume APIs (Application.Current.Suspending/Resuming, SuspendingEventHandler, SuspendingEventArgs) copied verbatim fail to compile against WinUI 3 Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Application, which removed them.
items.evidence: migration-score.json build_error ('Application.Suspending/Resuming not defined on WinUI 3 ... Scenario1_ConnectDisconnect.xaml.cs, EventHandlerForDevice.cs'); session-log grep shows App.Current.Suspending += / Resuming += and SuspendingEventHandler in EventHandlerForDevice.cs, Scenario1, Scenario4.
items.skill_search: grep for 'Suspending|Resuming|Suspend|lifecycle' across winui-uwp-migration; grep 'Suspend' in unsupported-api-inventory.json
items.root_cause: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md #lifecycle only covers OnLaunched/OnActivated/OnFileActivated; it never mentions the Suspending/Resuming events, and unsupported-api-inventory.json has no matching pattern, so Initialize injected no TODO and Validate flagged nothing.
items.proposed_fix: Add an 'adaptable' entry to unsupported-api-inventory.json (pattern matching Application.Current.Suspending/Resuming and SuspendingEventHandler/Args, anchor '#lifecycle') so Initialize injects a TODO at each call site, AND extend the #lifecycle section of MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md to state that WinUI 3 has no Suspending/Resuming and to relocate cleanup to Window.Closed / AppWindow.Closing.
items.generalizes: UWP apps and the entire UWP device-access sample family (USB/serial/HID/Bluetooth) ship EventHandlerForDevice with hardcoded suspend/resume wiring; suspend-based resource cleanup is a ubiquitous UWP idiom that always breaks the WinUI 3 build.
